title: Learning and Educating Project Managers in the Age of AI: Evidence and Implications for Competence Development
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing project work while raising questions about how project professionals acquire and demonstrate competence. This article develops an evidence-informed framework for learning and educating project managers in AI-enabled environments. It undertakes a focused integrative analysis of findings from a 2026 survey of 300 German project professionals and selected empirical studies of AI-assisted project work, learning, and education. In the source survey, 91% reported readiness to develop competences, learning-by-doing was the most highly rated individual format, and mentoring/coaching was the highest-rated organizational support measure. Experimental and classroom evidence indicates that AI can improve task performance and provide instructional scaffolding, but output improvements do not necessarily imply durable learning or sound contextual judgment. We propose a three-part educational architecture encompassing foundational project management judgment, responsible human–AI collaboration, and project value-oriented orchestration. It is operationalized through scaffolded practice, explicit AI-use rules, progressively independent assessments, and workplace-supported development. The framework is a conceptual synthesis, not an intervention validated by the source survey. The article offers testable propositions and an evaluation agenda for universities, employers, trainers, and professional associations.
